# Glassdoor.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/glassdoor-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/glassdoor-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects job listing data from Glassdoor.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Glassdoor (2025 update)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-glassdoor)
- **Code:** [`glassdoor.py`](glassdoor.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Job pages](results/jobs.json) · [Review pages](results/reviews.json) · [Salary pages](results/salaries.json) · [Companies](results/companies.json)

## What it scrapes

- Glassdoor company salary data
- Glassdoor company review data
- Glassdoor company job listing data

## Functions

- `scrape_jobs(url, max_pages=None)` → `List[Dict]`: Scrape Glassdoor job listing page for job listings (with pagination)
- `scrape_reviews(url, max_pages=None)` → `List[Dict]`: Scrape Glassdoor reviews listings from reviews page (with pagination)
- `scrape_salaries(url, max_pages=None)` → `Dict`: Scrape Glassdoor Salary page for salary listing data (with pagination)

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import glassdoor


async def main():
    jobs = await glassdoor.scrape_jobs(
        "https://www.glassdoor.com/Jobs/eBay-Jobs-E7853.htm?filter.countryId=1",
        max_pages=3,
    )
    salaries = await glassdoor.scrape_salaries(
        "https://www.glassdoor.com/Salary/eBay-Salaries-E7853.htm",
        max_pages=3,
    )
    reviews = await glassdoor.scrape_reviews(
        "https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/eBay-Reviews-E7853.htm",
        max_pages=3,
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`FoundCompany`**: `name`, `id`, `shortName`, `logoURL?`, `websiteURL?`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`glassdoor.py`](glassdoor.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/glassdoor-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_glassdoor_url`, `test_salary_range_parsing`, `test_find_companies`, `test_job_scraping`, `test_salary_scraping`, `test_review_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
